hypothesis: Shared contexts (several questions with different answers against one byte-identical context) remove the context->answer shortcut, so the model reads the question and RAG310 answerable accuracy rises.

data.shared-ctx-01: data/public-dialogue-shared-ctx-01 (scripts/prepare_contrastive_qa.py, built in the parallel answer-quality session): mix-04 real QA regrouped into 3,867 shared contexts, 11,969 real-QA rows (1,400 single-answer passages dropped), 1-3 passages per context.
data.mix06: data/public-dialogue-mix-06 = shared-ctx-01 + teacher-qa-kr-01-shared (3,152 rows, shared contexts of two korea.kr passages, 2-8 questions each) at 25% sampling mass.

recipe: Init pretrained base (runs/trid-korean-medium-cpt-gpu-complete), 3,000 steps, same seed/lr/batch as gpu-05-mix04-s3000, L40S shared with teacher generation. Evaluated on the GPU.
conclusion: At 3,000 steps the shared-context KLUE mix was significantly worse than mix-04 on RAG310 answerable (p=0.014) and did not raise question sensitivity (all_same 0.29 -> 0.36). Hypothesis not supported as built. Confounds: shared-ctx-01 drops 1,400 passages and 11% of real-QA rows and most contexts carry 2-3 passages (longer prompts, more distractors) while RAG310/sensitivity use the original layouts. Adding shared-context institution QA recovered the loss (p=0.047 vs shared-ctx-01) but is not better than mix-04 (p=0.78).
review: Automatic RAG310 and question-sensitivity scoring; public 8 by assistant review against predeclared facts, not independent human evaluation.
